_how_to_use: Add approved reviews to the TOP of the "reviews" list, in the same shape, without "sample": true. tool must be one of: Send, Pixel, Pinky, WinXP, Marketplace (Marketplace is shown as "sent4u"). rating is 1-5. text is up to 280 characters. The rating, review count and "would recommend" figures on the site are worked out from the real reviews here. The entries marked "sample": true are made-up placeholders and are NOT shown unless you set showSamples to true (only do that for a private preview, never on the live site).

reviews.name: Lena K.
reviews.text: I sent it with Pinky and she screenshotted the Yes button before she even replied. Instant hit.

reviews.name: Omar S.
reviews.text: Pixel’s little LCD look is perfect. She thought I had built a Game Boy app just for her.

reviews.name: Jordan M.
reviews.text: The XP desktop with the envelope on it made her laugh out loud. Best first message I have ever sent.

reviews.name: Aisha B.
reviews.text: The No button gets more dramatic every time you press it. He gave up on No in three taps.

reviews.name: Kenji T.
reviews.text: Cats on a pier, a snake game, and then a calendar invite. Very sweet. I would love a few more scenes.

reviews.name: Maya R.
reviews.text: She picked the place and the time, and it landed in her calendar. I did nothing after sending the link.

reviews.name: Ren A.
reviews.text: Eight links for less than ten dollars. I sent one to each of my friends as a joke, and one was for real.

reviews.name: Sofia P.
reviews.text: Black and neon pink, exactly her taste. She said yes, then sent the link to her sister.

reviews.name: Daniel W.
reviews.text: The retro XP window is a great touch. Editing the text right inside the invitation was easy.

reviews.name: Nora H.
reviews.text: I had five days to tweak the wording and I used all five. Worth it.

reviews.name: Ivan L.
reviews.text: The Nokia sound when the message arrives got me. She replied with three heart emojis.

reviews.name: Chloe D.
reviews.text: Sent a WinXP link and a Pixel link to two people, one each. Both said yes, oddly enough.
